summary.name: Edmund
summary.one_liner: Edmund is a minimal, file-based, native macOS Markdown editor with inline WYSIWYG live preview, released as open source under Apache 2.0.
use_cases: Editing Markdown notes as plain files on a Mac
Writing Markdown with inline live preview instead of split view
Using a standalone Markdown editor alongside an existing Markdown knowledge base
Writing documents with GFM, Mermaid diagrams and math
Reading Markdown in read mode and exporting to PDF
summary.what_it_does: Edmund is a native macOS Markdown editor built with AppKit and TextKit 2, with native toolbar, menus and integrations such as QuickLook and Finder actions. It renders Markdown inline as you type (WYSIWYG-style) and works directly on files, with no dedicated folders or vaults required. It supports GFM and about 99% of Obsidian-flavored Markdown, Mermaid diagrams, and math via KaTeX with an extension. Other features include find and replace, a read mode, and export to PDF. The page says data stays on the device with zero diagnostics, and the app is listed as free and open source under Apache 2.0.
notable: Inline WYSIWYG live preview similar to Typora and Obsidian
File-based with no vaults required; built with AppKit and TextKit 2 rather than Electron/WebKit
Compares itself with Typora, Obsidian, MacDown, MarkEdit, CotEditor, VS Code and others, listing a 16 MB app size
caveats: Folder support and file outline are planned, not yet available
Math support is listed as up to 99.5% KaTeX compatibility, not full
